subject: Renewal: usage & performance debrief — expansion path
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@primehealth.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gwen Park <gwen.park@primehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal health & usage report — PrimeHealth (DL-4387)

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Thanks for the support over the last year — the team and I pulled together a usage pack for May and a short ROI note for the execs. We're due to start renewal conversations in July and want to make sure we have an operational picture before pricing talks. Attached is the May usage export (token breakdown) and a latency snapshot from our staging traffic. Early notes:

- Overall token consumption up 32% month-over-month (driven by a new triage flow).
- P95 latency for our longest sequences rose from 420ms -> 620ms after the March model swap.
- We saw a spike of 3x in short-chat volume during two weekdays that impacted batching efficiency.

Primary asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the P95 increase is expected given the model variant we're on?
2) Recommendations for a commit size that balances our inflationary usage growth without overcommitting.
3) Any ops changes (batching, cache TTL) we should try before the renewal meeting on July 12.

I've attached the files referenced below. Gwen (cc) is our platform lead and will coordinate access to logs if needed.

Attachments: primehealth_usage_report_May2028.pdf (PDF), inference_latency_snapshot_May2028.csv (CSV)

Best,
Elena Novak
Head of Platform
PrimeHealth

---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health & usage report — PrimeHealth (DL-4387)

Elena — thanks for the package and the clear asks. We're looking through the CSV now. Quick take:

- The P95 bump aligns with the architecture change and the longer-context model you're on; the kernel selection shifts mean tail latency can increase for sequences >1k tokens. That's expected but not ideal.
- The short-chat surge suggests batching windows aren't well tuned for bursty traffic; we can reduce batching max-wait to improve latency at the cost of token efficiency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa and I will run a short ops experiment: decrease max_wait to 10ms for the chat route for 48 hours and monitor P50/P95 delta.
2) Ben, can you prepare two commit scenarios: a conservative renewal that matches current run-rate + 15% buffer, and an accelerated-commit that discounts burst credits for committed capacity?
3) I'll ask the SRE team to pull kernel profiling for the current model variant and share recommended quantization/compilation knobs that might shave P95.

Can we meet next Thursday (June 29) 10:30 PT for a quick sync before the July 12 renewal?

Thanks — Logan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health & usage report — PrimeHealth (DL-4387)

Elena / Logan — I ran the first-pass ops analysis against your May export and pulled a short experiment plan. Highlights:

- Root cause: the March model variant increased KV cache population per session which reduces batching density for short interactions. That explains the P95 fade when short-chat bursts occur.
- Quick wins (try immediately):
  * Drop chat route max_wait from 25ms -> 10ms for 48h (should recover P95 by ~120ms based on similar customers).
  * Increase prefix cache TTL for user sessions from 30m -> 2h to improve reuse.
  * Enable per-route continuous batching (we can toggle on/off per-route) to isolate impact.

I've attached a one-page playbook and an ops runbook for toggles. If you approve, SRE will run the change window on Monday and we'll monitor.

Proposed renewal options (high-level) for Ben to expand into price decks:
- Option A: Run-rate +15% commit (no change to SLA) — low risk, preserves current economics.
- Option B: Run-rate +30% commit with 10% committed-cap discount and 5% free burst credits — recommended if PrimeHealth expects continued growth from the new triage flow.
- Option C: Short-term bridge: 60-day temporary burst credits while we complete kernel/TL optimizations, then transition to Option B.

Elena — will you confirm if the triage flow will ship additional features in Q3? That will help Ben size the right commit.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Team — putting numbers against Marissa's options. Sketch below (full deck attached as link):

- Current run-rate (May avg): 2.1B tokens/mo
- Option A: 2.4B tokens/mo (run-rate +15%) — list price applies; renewal term 12 months; estimated monthly cost $128k
- Option B: 2.7B tokens/mo (run-rate +30%) — 10% discount on committed units + 5% burst credit pool; estimated monthly cost $115k after discount
- Option C: Bridge: 2.1B committed with a 60-day 20% burst credit pool for surges; convert to Option B after bridge period with a true-up.

Notes: Option B minimizes unit cost at the expense of higher commit. Option C reduces risk while we run the ops kernel optimizations and validate the P95 stability.

Next: Elena — if you confirm the Q3 triage roadmap (approx additional 18-25% token pressure), I'll prepare a redlines-ready amendment and a term sheet for July 12. Also proposed June 29 quick sync to validate the ops experiment results before the renewal.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
